title: Answer review 1 in the squash-chain landing design
summary: Revise docs/design/squash-chain-landing.md so it answers each finding of review 1 (3 major, 5 minor, 2 nit) and the review's three decisions, with a response appendix like the study-capability-m1 design. Documentation only; no code is built.

defaults_applied.how: Found the review file and design in the repository and inferred that answering means revising the design.
The design is revised and then reviewed again before any build job.
Each answer cites the code or doc it relies on, and untested claims are labeled.
One focused docs change; no code.
The verifier runs cargo test and fmt check, which include the wording scan.

assumptions: 'Answer review 1' means revising the design to respond to each finding of docs/design/reviews/squash-chain-landing-review-1.md, as was done for study-capability-m1 (response appendix in the design), not writing a new review.

The user did not answer the review's three decisions, so the producer picks and records defaults: record explicit order (predecessor field) in candidate.json; refuse chains whose jobs change classification rules files; refuse chain landing on commits with more than one parent.
The design stays proposed and no Rust is built.

acceptance_criteria.text: docs/design/squash-chain-landing.md is revised so every finding of review 1 (R1-M1, M2, M3, m1 to m5, n1, n2) is answered: fixed in the text, or declined with a stated reason.

The design has an appendix mapping each review 1 finding id to the section that answers it, and states the answer to the review's three decisions for the user (chain order, rules-file changes, merge commits), each as a stated assumption.

R1-M1: the chain order is defined unambiguously for reverting jobs and for jobs that change no governed content, either by a recorded predecessor or sequence field or by a stated refusal, with the cases added to the test list.
R1-M2: §3 B and §4.4 no longer claim the final verifier saw the whole tree. They say the benefit over option E is catching accidental mismatches, not forgery.
R1-M3: the design states which rules each recorded fingerprint uses and what happens when a job in the chain changes the path classification rules.

The minor findings are covered: jobs::check and history in the follow-up list, the merge-commit case, one schema choice reconciled with D69, partly landed chains, and one refusal test per per-job check on a middle job.

The change is documentation only: no Rust code, athena.toml, workflow, or records/ file is touched. A CHANGELOG line is added, and D69 in docs/decisions.md is amended only if the schema choice changes.
Run `cargo test --locked` (including xtask policy wording scan) and `cargo fmt --check`; both pass.

out_of_scope: Implementing the chain-aware landing rule in Rust
departures: Slightly higher cost than reference because a long design doc must be revised against 10 findings.
